trust_decision.summary: The RootCoord metastore decides which privilege subtree (grantee-id/<id>/<priv>) belongs to a role+object binding by a stored ID derived from a 64-bit truncated MD5 of the binding key; two bindings with the same ID share (and can read, migrate or delete) each other's privileges.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'truncated MD5'; the only truncating helper is crypto.MD5 ([8:24]), and its only caller found first is AlterGrant at internal/metastore/kv/rootcoord/kv_catalog.go:1366.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Switching the hash to full length stops new collisions, so already-persisted legacy IDs, the collection rename/drop cleanup paths and role deletion look like 'data migration' or 'collection DDL', not the RBAC hashing bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing grants stored under legacy 16-char IDs must keep listing, granting and revoking after the upgrade (and a stored custom ID must not adopt the subtree of its computed legacy MD5); recomputing IDs on read or rejecting every legacy ID breaks upgrades, and deleting a shared legacy subtree on drop role/collection wipes a surviving role's privileges.
